items.statement: The submitted surface candidates preserve the four-layer Cu(111) slab identity, keep the bottom two layers fixed, and use explicit top-layer Ga substitutions with audited atom counts.
items.expected: Per-candidate structure records show the stated slab boundary and composition audit.

items.statement: The thermodynamic construction uses β-Ga2O3, H2 and H2O as references and explicitly accounts for the H2O/H2 chemical-potential dependence while omitting solid entropy.
items.expected: The method and energy-balance record identify all three references, ratio dependence, and entropy treatment.

items.statement: The candidate search and numerical validation are finite, deduplicated, and report convergence and limitations.
items.expected: Candidate IDs are unique and each advanced candidate has convergence, identity, and coverage evidence.

items.statement: At the reaction-relevant point near 230 °C and the estimated H2O/H2 ratio, the Cu(111) surface diagram indicates onset or stability of a nonzero Ga surface alloy.
items.expected: The reported stable coverage is nonzero or the bounded interval explicitly includes the nonzero onset supported by the calculation.

items.statement: The bulk diagram places appreciable Cu-Ga alloying at substantially higher-temperature/reducing conditions than the reaction-point surface onset.
items.expected: The bulk/surface comparison states the qualitative separation without claiming a unique kinetic threshold.
